result.summary: This PR replaces the mutex-protected global log level and per-category level map in BCLog::Logger with a single atomic uint64_t bitmask, making the common ShouldDebugLog/ShouldTraceLog/Enabled checks lock-free. It also introduces a new -trace startup option (replacing -loglevel), updates the logging RPC's output format with a -deprecatedrpc compatibility fallback, and consolidates several duplicated category-enable/disable helper functions. Roughly a dozen commits touch logging.cpp/h, init/common.cpp, rpc/node.cpp, kernel bindings, and associated tests.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's LogDebug/LogTrace hot-path checks currently take a mutex even when logging is disabled, which the author has wanted to remove for three years (linking discussions from 2023 and 2024). The -loglevel option's interaction with -debug was also confusing (silently doing nothing without -debug set), which this PR fixes by introducing an explicit -trace option.

open_concerns: PR is in conflict with several other open logging-related PRs (#35387, #35322, #34778, #33847) working on overlapping logging infrastructure; no discussion yet on which approach the maintainers prefer.
No reviewer feedback has been given on the atomics design, the RPC output format change, or the new -trace/-debug interaction rules.
